model.frame: World-space tangent and bitangent are re-orthogonalized against the final normal and rotated around that normal
model.range: Material anisotropy is exposed in [-1,1] and internally clamped to [-0.9,0.9] for stable directional roughness
model.roughness: Positive anisotropy broadens alpha along tangent and narrows it along bitangent; negative anisotropy swaps the axes
model.distribution: Anisotropic Trowbridge-Reitz GGX uses TdotH, BdotH, NdotH and alphaT/alphaB
model.visibility: Correlated anisotropic Smith visibility uses projected view and light directions in the same tangent frame
model.fallback: Anisotropy zero delegates to the established isotropic GGX distribution and visibility path

invariants: The tangent frame is orthonormal to the final world-space normal and preserves mesh tangent handedness
Rotation changes highlight orientation without changing the normal or anisotropy magnitude
Positive and negative anisotropy swap the directional roughness axes
Anisotropy zero preserves the established isotropic GGX direct-light path
Snow coverage attenuates substrate anisotropy with the shared snow mask
All GGX denominators and directional alpha values have explicit lower bounds
limitations: The model uses mesh tangents and a scalar rotation instead of a flow map or strand direction texture
The internal anisotropy clamp limits magnitude to 0.9 to avoid singular highlights at the exposed endpoints
Visual confirmation and platform shader compilation still require a licensed Unity Editor
